q01.rationale: The party's own record abolished the consumer carbon tax: Finance Minister Bailey (Hansard 2026-02-18) treats its removal as settled and adjusts policy to it ('so when the carbon tax was removed'). No fetched source supports reinstating; mapping a record statement to strong opposition took judgment.

q03.rationale: No fetched source names a wealth tax on personal fortunes — the statement's instrument. The party's own words promise only unspecified taxes/'fair share' for 'those at the very top' (goal-level), and the only 'wealth tax package' language is the BC Green caucus's and its characterization of the government, both excluded by CODEBOOK §5.

q04.rationale: Steve Morissette's Budget 2026 speech (Hansard 2026-02-19) states plainly this is not an austerity budget and that Budget 2026 does not cut services; the 2026 campaign (ndp-0002/0003, 2026-09-22) frames 'make cuts' as the wrong choice. Document date 2026-02-19; corroborated by campaign-era material.

q10.rationale: Policy page 'Results for You' (document date 2024-01-04) records the province removing barriers to deliver more homes near transit hubs — housing near transit over local rules — but without the statement's 'require'/'higher-density' wording, so the weaker value. Pre-campaign document; not clearly corroborated 2026, so at most medium.

q11.rationale: No fetched source addresses expanding rent-control coverage to more rental units. Capping rent increases well below inflation and the Rental Protection Fund (ndp-0013) are adjacent instruments, not the statement's instrument (coverage expansion), so §5 null.
